title: Add percentile skyline panel and noisy neighbor detector
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: Long-tail token-cost and latency regressions are often visible only in higher percentiles and across route cohorts. Existing dashboards surface P50/P95 but it's difficult to compare shapes across routes and identify when GPU queueing or kernel warmup on noisy tenants is the root cause. This PR introduces a percentile skyline visualization and a lightweight noisy-neighbor detector service that correlates GPU queueing and kernel-queue metrics with invocation traces to surface tenants or workloads causing contention.

What this changes: 1) New Grafana dashboard panel 'Percentile Skyline' that draws stacked percentile curves (P50/P75/P90/P95/P99) per-route with normalized x-axis (tokens) so teams can compare prompt shapes side-by-side. 2) Noisy-neighbor detector: a small service that consumes kernel-queue and GPU-queue histograms + sampled traces and emits 'noisy_neighbor' events when correlation and temporal alignment exceed thresholds. 3) Alert tuning: an adaptive alert that suppresses noisy-neighbor alerts during planned capacity changes and auto-quiet windows; also adds an annotation join to the skyline panel to mark noisy-neighbor events. 4) Observability proxy changes: metric labels are enriched with route fingerprint and short invocation signature to make percentile rollups per-route efficient.

Implementation notes: - The detector runs as a new K8s deployment under observability namespace with a single replica by default. It uses a sliding-window Pearson correlation across kernel_queue_ms and invocation_wait_ms histograms. Thresholds are feature-flagged and stored in feature-config (defaults conservative). - The skyline panel leverages downsampled percentile rollups from metric-rollup-service to avoid large query costs; it requests P50..P99 over token-bucket windows. - We added a small shim in the trace-forwarder to attach invocation short-id to metric points for easier join.

Checklist: - [x] Dashboard JSON and panel templates added - [x] Noisy neighbor detector service + K8s manifest - [x] Unit tests for correlation logic - [x] Integration test that simulates queued kernels and verifies alert emission - [x] Feature-flag gating and rollout steps documented - [x] Migration notes for metric-rollup-service label change

Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature-flag, deploy detector to staging, run a 72h watch with synthetic noisy tenants (script included). - If stable, roll out to canary region with single replica and increase retention from 24h->72h for metric rollups. - After 2 weeks, evaluate false positive rate; tune thresholds or disable auto-escalation.

Related: Linear ENG-4312 (percentile skyline dashboard), ENG-4320 (noisy neighbour detection prototype). Support ticket SUP-1298 provided synthetic traces used in integration tests.

Notes on safety and cost: Skyline queries use downsampled rollups; added safeguards to cap query cardinality. Detector emits lightweight events only when correlation sustained > 3 windows.

release_notes:
- Added a new 'Percentile Skyline' dashboard panel to visualize P50/P75/P90/P95/P99 across routes and token positions.
- Introduced a noisy-neighbor detector service that correlates GPU/kernel queue metrics with invocation traces to detect tenants causing contention.
- Added alert tuning with auto-quiet windows and dashboard annotations for detected events.
- Note: rollout is behind feature-flag; metric-rollup label changes require migration steps described in docs/observability/percentile_skyline_readme.md
